name: Open a bottle using ordinary objects
blurb: A lever and a fulcrum. Once you understand the mechanics, almost any rigid object with an edge becomes a bottle opener.
gear: Lighters, spoons, keys, a table edge, paper
steps: Understand the principle: grip the bottle neck firmly with one hand, place a rigid edge under the cap’s crimp, and lever downwards against your index finger as the fulcrum.
Learn the lighter method, which is the most reliable and works with almost any rigid object.
Learn the spoon and the key variants, which use exactly the same mechanics.
Learn the paper method, where a folded sheet becomes rigid enough to act as the lever.
Learn the counter-edge method, which needs a downward strike and a surface you are allowed to damage.
Practise until it takes one motion rather than five attempts.
tips: Grip the neck tightly right under the cap. A loose grip is why it slips and why hands get cut.
Never use your teeth. Dentists see this injury constantly.
Do not damage someone else’s furniture for a party trick.
proof: You open a bottle with three different everyday objects, one motion each.
